- When sentiment is positive (≥0.0), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.1), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward.
- Forecast bias is more pronounced in early 30-day window; apply stronger correction for first 7–10 days.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to catch momentum; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; lagged sentiment (2–3 days ago) is more reliable for correction.
